purpose: Pilot-derived human-review regression examples for the minimum valid syntactic-semantic chunk objective. Suggested spans are review targets, not universal gold boundaries or forced templates.

cases.issue: misassigned / duplicated family meaning across adjacent spans
cases.review_target: Keep negation, verb, and subject aligned; do not translate words 61-62 as 'family' and word 63 as 'their family'.
Do not output a fragment like 'Then if is'; preserve the relation between the conditional particle, verb, subject and predicate.
'And call to witness' followed by 'two witnesses' should be reconsidered as the smallest complete local verb-object unit.

cases.issue: conditional subject/predicate and reciprocal reminder relationship
cases.review_target: Do not leave 'so that if errs' separated from 'one of the two'; preserve who errs and who reminds.

cases.issue: relative clause split across the complement
cases.review_target: Do not isolate 'of what' from the words that identify what was left and by whom.

cases.issue: passive predicate and post-verbal subject ordering
cases.review_target: The Arabic order may differ from English order; keep the meaning 'a group is thrown into it' aligned to the full local span.
Do not leave 'then it' without the verb 'sways' where the local construction requires the complete unit.

cases.issue: predicate separated from its post-verbal subject
cases.review_target: Check the verb 'will be distressed' with 'the faces of those who disbelieved'.
Do not make 'if', 'your water becomes', and 'sunken' disconnected fragments when the conditional proposition is the minimum valid unit.
